problems.field: studies[S1].arms[No-AI].description (the same claim recurs in eligibility.reason, open_questions[0], and reconciliation.agreed_fields_checked, field 'Practice task with AI before both conditions')
problems.form_value: Every participant had used ChatGPT in the practice story before either condition.
problems.source_says: The paper says every participant completed a practice story structured like the AI-help condition, with ChatGPT available and prompting suggestions shown, and calls it an opportunity to get familiar with LLM prompting. It never says that each participant sent ChatGPT a message, and the AI-help screen sets no minimum ('send as many messages as you need'). In the main AI-help task, Figure 3 (left panel) plots a column of participants at an integration score of 0.0, so an instruction to use ChatGPT did not guarantee use. Supported wording: every participant completed a practice story with ChatGPT available before either condition. Criterion 1 is unaffected.
problems.quote: The practice story-writing was included to ensure participants with no experience working with LLM chatbots had an opportunity to familiarize themselves with the nuances of LLM prompting.
problems.locator: PDF p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task, last paragraph; PDF p. 32, Appendix A (screen text); PDF p. 16, Figure 3, left panel

confirmed.statement: (a) The paper states random assignment once: 'The order of presentation was randomized, such that an equal number of participants completed the AI-help and No-AI conditions first.' No other passage describes how conditions were allocated (the other 'random' hits are the ICC model and the random intercepts), and the mechanism is not described. The form's assignment quote is verbatim. The form is also right that 'an equal number' cannot be exact for 391 or 263, and the paper gives no count by order.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Method, Story Writing Task; page-level search of PDF pp. 1-34 for 'random' (pp. 9, 14, 18, and one reference title on p. 28)

confirmed.statement: (e) Within-person design with randomized order: 'We employ a within-subjects design, where participants write two stories with and without AI assistance.' Each of the 263 contributes one story per condition (paired t-tests with df = 262). randomized = yes, unit = within_person_order, and structure = within (the paper's own term) are supported, and the codebook accepts this design for criterion 1.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, The Present Research; PDF p. 9, Method, Story Writing Task; PDF p. 14 and p. 17, Results

confirmed.statement: The two prompts were 'selected and counterbalanced across conditions: pen-paper-write and year-week-embark'. This is the only mention of counterbalancing, and the paper does not say how it was done, as what_was_assigned says.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Method, Story Writing Task (only hit for 'counterbalanc')

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is access to ChatGPT for the participant's own story: 'For the AI-help condition, participants were instructed to collaborate with ChatGPT during the story writing task (Appendix A). Participants were provided two textboxes, one to communicate with ChatGPT and the other to input and submit their story.' Copy-paste was disabled across the website. Both conditions score the participant's own submitted story, so no condition differs only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task; PDF p. 32, Appendix A; PDF p. 14, Results, Story Originality

confirmed.statement: (b) The contrast is access, not mandated use. The AI-help screen asks participants to 'send as many messages as you need to complete your story', with no minimum. The integration correlation keeps all 263 participants (t(261)), and Figure 3 plots a column of them at 0.0, which the paper does not explain. The form's AI-help description ('could chat freely') codes access, which fits.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 32, Appendix A (screen text); PDF pp. 14-15, Results, Story Originality; PDF p. 16, Figure 3, left panel

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is generative AI: 'A custom API was used to call ChatGPT based on the GPT 3.5 base model.' The paper calls it 'the LLM chatbot'. A hidden system prompt set it up as a creativity support tool and constrained its output to bullet points. name_model is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task; PDF p. 8, The Present Research

confirmed.statement: ai_tool.role open_chat and how_used match the text: 'When provided AI assistance, we allowed participants to freely interact with the LLM chatbot'. The hidden system prompt, the bullet-point limit, the copy-paste block, the 'source of ideas' instruction, and the practice story (50 words minimum, 2 minutes recommended, structured like the AI-help condition) are all as how_used says.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, The Present Research; PDF p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task; PDF p. 11, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm matches the form: 'The visual features of the No-AI condition were matched to the AI-help condition, except the ChatGPT textbox was removed and only the story writing textbox was displayed'. Appendix B shows no aid. The only extra element is an instruction to pose the practice prompting strategies to oneself 'as a form of brainstorming', placed in the practice paragraph. It is an instruction, not web search, examples, or a partner, so ai = none and ai_vs_bau fit.

confirmed.statement: design_class online_rct fits: the 391 students took part 'in the online study', run on Qualtrics and a custom website. The paper reports no analysis by order, so the form's carryover open question stands.

summary: The PDF states once (p. 9) that the order of the AI-help and No-AI story conditions was randomized in a within-subjects design, so each of the 263 analyzed students wrote one story with access to a GPT-3.5 chatbot limited to bullet-point ideas and one in a matched interface without it, which meets criterion 1 under the codebook's within-person rule. One detail is not supported: the No-AI arm description (repeated in eligibility.reason and open_questions) says every participant used ChatGPT in the practice story, but the paper says only that everyone completed a practice structured like the AI-help condition, as an opportunity to get familiar with LLM prompting.
